                  6600.0 019FA036-54B5-7D2E-B6F5-1432548C74FB NULL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             "I want to be precise about what I had in front of me when I refused. I am not a lawyer, and I will not perform being one.

"Here is the answer I actually have.

"I looked at the address. Same district. I had stood a perimeter in that district seventy-two hours earlier and listened to forty-three people stop being voices. I had written an after-action report nobody asked me to sign. And the same commanding officer who ordered that operation was handing me a second building in the same sector — no brief, no parameters, no instruction to confirm who was inside.

"You learn to read an order the way you learn to read weather. Not from one fact. From the shape of several together. A brief that is missing tells you as much as a brief that is full. The thing they leave out is the thing they do not want documented. No civilian-verification requirement, seventy-two hours after forty-three civilians, is not an oversight. It is a decision. I had run enough operations to know which corners get cut by accident and which get cut on purpose, and a verification requirement is never cut by accident. It is the corner you cut when you have already decided what you are going to find."                   6800.0 019FA036-54B5-7D6C-8EC6-78254819825B NULL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             "So. "I refused. That is the insubordination charge.

"I want to say something about the word. Insubordination. The file says I disobeyed a lawful order from a superior, and on the narrow facts of the morning, that is true. I was given an order and I did not carry it out. But that is the institution choosing the smallest true word it can find. Insubordination is a discipline problem. It lives in the conduct manual next to dress violations and missed musters. It is a word you can close a file with. What I did was not a discipline problem. I declined to bring a powered frame to a building because I believed the man who sent me there meant to do again what he had already done once. The institution cannot write that sentence in a charge sheet. It has no box for it. So it reached for the box it had. Insubordination is what you call conscience when you have decided not to call it conscience — because the right word would make you ask what the order was for, and the question after that one is a question Halcyon was never going to put on a form."
